To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

OmpA forms temperature‐sensitivemulti‐state channels in bilayers, that OmpA channels are flexible proteins that exist as small and large pores, and that the transition from the small to large pore occurs between 22 and34°C.
OmpA forms two interconvertible channel states and that the ratio of the two channel states is temperature dependent, particularly at temperatures below 34°C.
outer membrane protein A of E. coli forms temperature‐dependent channels in planar bilayer membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism by which outer membranes regulate the passage of solutes across the outer membrane.
the study of the structure and function of the outer membrane protein, OmpA.
the study of the temperature dependence of single channel conductance and open probabilities for OmpA in planar lipid membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OmpA protein is a temperature‐sensitive pore‐forming protein that exists as two interconvertible states.
OmpA has the capacity to form a small and a large channel, but that the relative proportions of the channels depend upon the temperature.
OmpA exists in a flexible structure that can exist in two interconvertible conformations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
outer membrane proteins are temperature sensitive and that the temperature dependence of outer membrane protein function is a general phenomenon.
the OmpA channel is a flexible protein that is capable of forming two interconvertible pore structures.
the temperature‐sensitive channel is formed by a flexible protein that is able to change its structure and pore size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the outer membrane of E. coli is more flexible and less stable than previously thought.
the OmpA channel is temperature sensitive.

OmpA, a protein that has been studied for decades in the context of its function as a pore in the outer membrane of Gram‐negative bacteria, is in fact an unusual protein that forms temperature‐sensing pores.
